title: Paul Arrives in Jerusalem, Arrested in the Temple

questions.question: The prophet Agabus came down from Judea, took Paul's belt, bound his own hands and feet with it, and said what?
options: "Thus says the Holy Spirit, 'This is how the Jews at Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt and deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.'"
"A great imprisonment awaits you in Rome if you proceed to Jerusalem."
"The Spirit warns you: do not go to Jerusalem or you will not return."
"God has shown me chains and prison for you in the holy city."
questions.correctAnswer: "Thus says the Holy Spirit, 'This is how the Jews at Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt and deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.'"
questions.explanation: Acts 21:11 (ESV): "And coming to us, he took Paul's belt and bound his own feet and hands and said, 'Thus says the Holy Spirit, 'This is how the Jews at Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt and deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.'"

questions.question: The disciples urged Paul not to go to Jerusalem. What was Paul's response?
options: "What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be imprisoned but even to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."
"I know what awaits me, but God's call cannot be ignored."
"The Spirit compels me; no power on earth can stop me now."
"My life is in God's hands; I go where he sends regardless."
questions.correctAnswer: "What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be imprisoned but even to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."
questions.explanation: Acts 21:13 (ESV): "Then Paul answered, 'What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be imprisoned but even to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.'"

questions.question: When Paul arrived in Jerusalem, he met with James and the elders. What did they ask Paul to do to show he still lived in observance of the law?
options: Join four men under a vow, pay for their purification rites, and go to the temple to show he kept the law
Offer a sacrifice at the temple and receive the blessing of the high priest
Circumcise Timothy publicly to demonstrate his commitment to the law
Attend the Passover feast in Jerusalem according to the Mosaic tradition
questions.correctAnswer: Join four men under a vow, pay for their purification rites, and go to the temple to show he kept the law
questions.explanation: Acts 21:23-24 (ESV): "...we have four men who are under a vow; take these men and purify yourself along with them and pay their expenses, so that they may shave their heads. Thus all will know that there is nothing in what they have been told about you, but that you yourself also live in observance of the law."

questions.question: What false accusation did the Jews from Asia make when they saw Paul in the temple?
options: That he had brought Trophimus the Ephesian (a Gentile) into the temple
That he had spoken blasphemy against Moses and the Law
That he had defiled the offering of the men under the vow
That he had prevented circumcision among the Jewish diaspora
questions.correctAnswer: That he had brought Trophimus the Ephesian (a Gentile) into the temple
questions.explanation: Acts 21:28-29 (ESV): "...This is the man who is teaching everyone everywhere against the people and the law and this place. Moreover, he even brought Greeks into the temple and has defiled this holy place." For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city.

questions.question: The crowd was beating Paul when the Roman tribune and soldiers arrived. What did the tribune do?
options: Arrested Paul, bound him with chains, and asked who he was and what he had done
Rescued Paul and asked him privately what the disturbance was about
Ordered the crowd dispersed with force and brought Paul to safety
Had Paul flogged to discover the cause of the uproar quickly
questions.correctAnswer: Arrested Paul, bound him with chains, and asked who he was and what he had done
questions.explanation: Acts 21:33 (ESV): "Then the tribune came up and arrested him and ordered him to be bound with two chains. He inquired who he was and what he had done."

questions.question: At what place did the disciples urge Paul on his way south not to go to Jerusalem according to the Spirit?
options: Tyre
Sidon
Caesarea
Ptolemais
questions.explanation: Acts 21:4 (ESV): "And having sought out the disciples, we stayed there for seven days. And through the Spirit they were telling Paul not to go on to Jerusalem."

questions.question: Paul stayed with a man named Philip in Caesarea. Who was Philip?
options: The evangelist, one of the seven deacons
Philip the apostle, one of the twelve
Philip, a merchant from the city of Caesarea
Philip, a converted Pharisee who knew Paul from his youth
questions.correctAnswer: The evangelist, one of the seven deacons
questions.explanation: Acts 21:8 (ESV): "On the next day we departed and came to Caesarea, and we entered the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him."

questions.question: Philip had four unmarried daughters. What gift did they have?
options: The gift of prophecy
The gift of healing
The gift of tongues
The gift of teaching
questions.explanation: Acts 21:9 (ESV): "He had four unmarried daughters, who prophesied."

questions.question: After they could not dissuade Paul from going, the disciples said what?
options: "Let the will of the Lord be done."
"God's purposes cannot be thwarted."
"May God protect you in all your ways."
"We trust you to the care of our Father."
questions.correctAnswer: "Let the will of the Lord be done."
questions.explanation: Acts 21:14 (ESV): "And since he would not be persuaded, we ceased and said, 'Let the will of the Lord be done.'"

questions.question: James and the elders rejoiced over what Paul reported when he arrived in Jerusalem. What was this?
options: What God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry
The number of churches planted across Asia and Europe
The offering Paul brought from the Gentile churches
The conversion of Sergius Paulus and other Roman officials
questions.correctAnswer: What God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry
questions.explanation: Acts 21:19-20 (ESV): "After greeting them, he related one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry. And when they heard it, they glorified God."

questions.question: The Jerusalem elders noted that there were many thousands of Jewish believers who were zealous for the law. What rumor had they heard about Paul?
options: That he was teaching all the Jews among the Gentiles to forsake Moses and not circumcise their children
That he was collecting tithes from Jewish believers for a treasury in Antioch
That he was telling Gentiles they did not need to respect Jewish customs at all
That he planned to bring Trophimus into the temple court of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: That he was teaching all the Jews among the Gentiles to forsake Moses and not circumcise their children
questions.explanation: Acts 21:21 (ESV): "and they have been told about you that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or walk according to our customs."

questions.question: As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he asked the tribune for permission to speak to the people. The tribune was surprised to find Paul could speak what language?
options: Greek
Latin
Aramaic
Hebrew
questions.explanation: Acts 21:37 (ESV): "As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he said to the tribune, 'May I say something to you?' And he said, 'Do you speak Greek?'"

questions.question: The tribune confused Paul with an Egyptian who had led a revolt. How many men did the tribune think that Egyptian had led into the wilderness?
options: Four thousand men of the Assassins
Ten thousand armed rebels
Seven thousand followers to the Mount of Olives
Three thousand insurrectionists from the desert regions
questions.correctAnswer: Four thousand men of the Assassins
questions.explanation: Acts 21:38 (ESV): "Are you not the Egyptian, then, who recently stirred up a revolt and led the four thousand men of the Assassins out into the wilderness?"

questions.question: Paul described himself to the tribune. What did he say he was?
options: "A Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no obscure city."
"A Roman citizen by birth, trained under Gamaliel."
"An apostle of Jesus Christ, called by God's grace."
"A former Pharisee, now a minister of the Lord Jesus."
questions.correctAnswer: "A Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no obscure city."
questions.explanation: Acts 21:39 (ESV): "Paul replied, 'I am a Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no obscure city. I beg you, permit me to speak to the people.'"

questions.question: When Paul began to speak to the crowd in the Hebrew language, what happened?
options: They became even more quiet
They began shouting again
They threw things at him
They listened respectfully at first then turned hostile
questions.explanation: Acts 21:40 (ESV): "And when he had given him permission, Paul, standing on the steps, motioned with his hand to the people. And when there was a great hush, he addressed them in the Hebrew language..."

key_verse_text: "I am ready not only to be imprisoned but even to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."
